summary: David says is there yet any left of house of Saul that I may show kindness (hesed) for Jonathan's sake? Ziba servant of Saul says Jonathan has son lame in both feet in Lo-debar. David sends and brings him from Lo-debar: Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul comes falls on face does obeisance, David says Mephibosheth, fear not I will show kindness for Jonathan your father and restore all land of Saul your father and you shall eat bread at my table continually. Mephibosheth says what is your servant that you should look on such dead dog as I am? David calls Ziba all that pertained to Saul and house I give to master's son, you and sons and servants till land bring in that master's son may have food to eat, but Mephibosheth shall eat at my table continually. Ziba had 15 sons 20 servants, says according to all lord commands will servant do. So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem eating at king's table continually lame in both feet.
whyItMatters: Picture of grace to enemy's descendant — Mephibosheth crippled, living in Lo-debar (no pasture), called dead dog, yet brought to king's table like one of king's sons because of Jonathan's covenant, not his merit. Image of grace.

keyVerses.text: David said, “Is there yet any who is left of Saul’s house, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”
keyVerses.why: Motive — kindness for Jonathan's sake, not Mephibosheth's merit.

keyVerses.text: He bowed down, and said, “What is your servant, that you should look at such a dead dog as I am?”
keyVerses.why: Mephibosheth self-view — dead dog, crippled, enemy line.

keyVerses.text: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king’s table. He was lame in both his feet.
keyVerses.why: Ending image — lame both feet yet eating at king's table continually.

questions.question: Who is Mephibosheth and why lame?
questions.answer: Son of Jonathan, grandson of Saul, injured at age 5 when nurse fled after Saul and Jonathan died in battle (4:4 nurse fell, became lame). Lived in Lo-debar — means no pasture, desolate place beyond Jordan. Lame in both feet — cannot walk, dependent, unable to work. Grandson of king living in obscurity, fearing new king will kill remaining Saulide to secure throne (common practice). So call from king likely terrifying, not hopeful initially.

questions.question: What does 'show kindness for Jonathan's sake' and 'dead dog' mean?
questions.answer: Kindness = hesed — loyal lovingkindness, covenant loyalty beyond duty. For Jonathan's sake — because of covenant between David and Jonathan (1 Sam 20). Mephibosheth not rewarded for own merit but because of father's friendship. He says what is your servant that you should look on such dead dog as I am? Dead dog = self-deprecation, unclean animal, worthless, enemy. Contrast: king says you shall eat at my table continually like one of sons — adoption to table, not just field restored but fellowship at table despite lameness. Image of grace to undeserving, unable, enemy line for another's sake.

questions.question: Why does Ziba continue tilling land and sons servants?
questions.answer: Ziba was servant of house of Saul, with 15 sons 20 servants. David gives him all Saul's land to work so master's son may have food to eat, but Mephibosheth himself eats at king's table — meaning Ziba manages estate providing income while Mephibosheth enjoys fellowship. Mephibosheth dwelt Jerusalem eating continually at table, though lame both feet — lameness mentioned at start and end, not healed, but included despite. Shows inclusion not based on ability.

glossary.def: Loyal lovingkindness, covenant loyalty beyond duty, for Jonathan's sake.
No pasture, desolate place, no thing — where Mephibosheth lived.
